source_evidence: Series I Bonds offer a fixed rate of interest, adjusted for inflation.
answer: Series I U.S. Savings Bonds are inflation-indexed: they offer a fixed rate of interest that is adjusted for inflation. They are sold at face value, and you can buy up to $10,000 in face value of Series I bonds in a calendar year. If you redeem them during the first five years, you forfeit the interest for the three most recent months; after five years, there is no redemption penalty.
